I grow them in a zone 7.They like it cool, very moist, and shady but I can't tell you what the range would be. If other mushrooms grow around your area your probably good, or you could call you local mycological association and ask them.
Zone 7 doesn't really dip below freezing, I live in a zone 3 (4a/3b), would the fungus survive a winter if the proper humidity levels were present for the summer?

OK, so I looked around and can't find anything that specifically says what zone they grow in, but I did find some indirect information.

One source said that they should be below the average snow line during the winter to protect from harsh winter winds. They also are found wild in the Hokkaido region of Japan which is the northernmost area of the country and has the harshest weather. I also looked up some mushroom species that grow in Canada, and at least in Ontario many of the same species which grow in my region are present. So I would say you could probably grow them.

If your still worried you could always keep a log in you bathroom during the winter if you heat your house. The shower steam would give it the water it needs (mostly) and keep it out of the elements.
